The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voting Index (PVI) is a measure of how strongly a congressional district leans toward the Democratic or Republican party. It is calculated by comparing a district's vote in the past two presidential elections to the national average. The PVI is displayed as a letter (D or R) followed by a number, which indicates the number of percentage points above the national average that a district voted for the corresponding party. The formula for calculating PVI values was updated in 2022 to give more weight to the most recent presidential election.

Trans broken arm syndrome is a form of discrimination in which a doctor mistakenly assumes that a trans person's medical ailments are related to their trans status and treats them incorrectly or denies them care as a result. This can cause trans patients to hide their trans status when seeking medical care, particularly in rural or conservative areas. A 2022 survey from the Center for American Progress found that 19% of trans individuals had experienced this form of discrimination in the past year.

Transgender people have the right to medical privacy, which is protected by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). This means that medical providers and insurance companies are prohibited from disclosing personal medical information, including a person's transgender status, without their consent. HIPAA also allows transgender people to access and receive copies of their medical records from healthcare facilities.

It can be difficult for transgender people to find insurance coverage for medical needs related to gender transition, such as hormone therapy and sex reassignment surgery (SRS). This is because some insurance companies may view these treatments as cosmetic, experimental, or unnecessary, even though there is medical consensus that they are medically necessary for many transgender people. Courts have recognized gender dysphoria as a legitimate medical condition and have ruled that these treatments may be medically necessary. The ban on Medicare coverage for gender reassignment surgery was repealed by the US Department of Health and Human Services in 2014, but insurance companies still have the authority to decide whether to cover such procedures.
